A battery shows an abnormal heating precursor. Readings look normal for a while. At inspection, should we still flag it?

Synthetic precursor-memory task: the warning is a token, not a real temperature forecast. Both models see identical inputs and training examples.

Sequence & architecture

3 input features · 1 recurrent layer. The threshold is a task policy; initialization controls set starting parameters.

Training & convergence

Full-batch SGD. Each epoch averages one healthy and one warning sequence. Stop at the loss target, a plateau, or the epoch limit. A plateau is not successful convergence.

Starting weights are chosen to reveal the memory mechanism. Training updates all parameters using actual backpropagation.

Parameters & values
Hyperparameters

The model and its weights

Input order: [warning precursor, normal reading, inspection query]. Warning = [1,0,0], normal = [0,1,0], query = [0,0,1]. A healthy sequence starts with a normal reading. Initial hidden and cell states are zero; parameters are shared across time.

RNN: hₜ = tanh(Wᵣxₜ + Uᵣhₜ₋₁ + bᵣ). LSTM: f, i, o = σ(Wx + Uh + b), g = tanh(Wgx + Ugh + bg), cₜ = fₜ ⊙ cₜ₋₁ + iₜ ⊙ gₜ, hₜ = oₜ ⊙ tanh(cₜ).

Readout: z = vᵀhT + bᵧ, p = σ(z). Loss: −y log(p) − (1−y) log(1−p). Label y = 1 for a warning, 0 for healthy. The inspection threshold affects the decision, not the loss.

Backpropagation includes the full recurrent chain rule and indirect gate paths. The green line highlights the direct LSTM memory path: its local factor is fₜ. This is not the full recurrent Jacobian. LSTMs can still have exploding gradients; clipping is an additional remedy.

Clipping rescales the entire averaged gradient if its norm exceeds the limit. SGD updates every parameter. Changed settings may change which model succeeds; outcomes are calculated, never forced.
